newsitem.title: FINLAND: Current upsets no threat to EMU - Finnish official.
newsitem.headline: Current upsets no threat to EMU - Finnish official.

text.p: Current qualms over a European single currency in France and Germany are not obstacles to implementing EMU, a Finnish member of the European Union's monetary committee said on Thursday.

"They are no threat," finance ministry permanent under-secretary of state Johnny Akerholm, one of two Finnish members of the European Union's monetary committee, told Reuters after addressing a seminar. "The situation is still unchanged."
Asked if conflict in Germany over the revaluation of gold reserves or a possible victory for French socialists in elections on Sunday were a threat to the EMU process, he said:
"We will see plenty of discussions like this in the year to come and every time people will believe that something fundamental has happened."
On the chance that Sweden may decide to stay out of the first round of EMU, he repeated that this would not affect Finland's own commitment to join.
"Finland's point of departure has been all along that Finland draws its own conclusions based on its own conditions and does not depend on Sweden's choice," he said.
"If one thought differently one would see benefits in remaining outside, but there are in fact rather disadvantages in remaining outside."
